title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section (9) of a provisional plan for 'Paradigmes des courbes algébriques', listing the basic schemes and topoi of the theory. These are the modular topoi (moduli stacks) T_{0,ν} of genus-0 curves with ν marked points, over Q and over Q̄.

The previous page treats the degenerate cases ν = 0, 1, 2. There T_{0,ν} is not a scheme-like ('étendu') topos but a classifying topos, B_{Aut(P^1, marked points)}: B_PGL(2) (written GL(2)), B_Aff(1), B_{G_m}. ν = 3 gives the final topos e = Spec Q.

This page begins by noting that the fundamental groups are trivial, 'en profini aussi': π_1(T_{0,ν}) = 0 for 0 ≤ ν ≤ 3. In modern terms, π_1^et(BG) = π_0(G) = 1 for a connected group G, and M_{0,3} is a point. The higher homotopy is not trivial (π_2 = π_1(G)), and the page does not mention this.

For ν ≥ 4, T_{0,ν} is (equivalent to) the scheme of configurations (x_1, …, x_{ν-3}) of ν-3 distinct points in P^1 − {0,1,∞} = A^1 − {0,1}. This is the usual normalisation that sends the first three marked points to 0, 1, ∞.

Its (geometric) fundamental group is the profinite completion of a 'braid group' Π_{0,ν}. In modern terms this is the pure mapping class group of the sphere with ν punctures, i.e. the pure spherical braid group modulo its centre. Like every 'groupe cartésien', Π_{0,ν} depends contravariantly on the finite set [1,ν] with respect to monomorphisms. This functoriality comes from the point-forgetting maps M_{0,ν} → M_{0,μ} induced by injections [1,μ] ↪ [1,ν].

Finally, since the T_{0,ν} are defined over Q and the symmetric group S_ν acts on them by permuting the marked points, the group S_ν × Γ acts on the geometric topos (T_{0,ν})_{Q̄}, where Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). This induces outer actions on the profinite braid groups, compatible with the forgetful functoriality.

The page sets up the genus-0 part of the 'Teichmüller tower' with its Galois action. The next page states the arithmetic-geometric conjecture: the homomorphism π_1(M_{g,ν}) → Autextloc(π_1(curve minus points)), i.e. what became the anabelian / Galois–Teichmüller programme.
errors: Calling π_1(M_{0,ν}) a 'groupe de tresses' is loose. It is the pure mapping class group of the ν-punctured sphere (pure sphere braid group mod centre Z/2), not an Artin braid group.

π_1 = 0 for ν ≤ 3 is correct, but the ν ≤ 2 stacks have nontrivial π_2 (e.g. π_2(B_{G_m}) = Ẑ(1), π_2(B_{PGL_2}) = Z/2). So 'triviality' holds only at the π_1 level, which is presumably all that is intended.
Previous page writes B_GL(2) where the automorphism group of P^1 is PGL(2) (minor slip).

Strictly, the S_ν × Γ action is on the topos / stack, and only an outer action on π_1 unless a base point (e.g. a tangential one) is chosen. The page does not address this; the next page does, via 'Autext'.

ideas.what: Moduli stack of genus 0 curves with ν ≤ 3 points is a classifying stack with trivial π_1; M_{0,3} = point
ideas.modern_name: M_{0,n} for n<3 as BG; étale homotopy of classifying stacks

ideas.what: M_{0,ν} ≅ configuration space of ν−3 distinct points in P^1 − {0,1,∞}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}

ideas.what: Profinite completion of the genus-0 mapping class ('braid') group as π_1 of M_{0,ν} over Q̄, functorial contravariantly in [1,ν] under injections (forgetful maps)
ideas.modern_name: genus-0 Teichmüller tower; point-forgetting maps; an FI^op-group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981)

ideas.what: Action of S_ν × Gal(Q̄/Q) on (M_{0,ν})_{Q̄} and hence (outer) on its profinite π_1
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the Teichmüller tower / Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory

deep.surprise_reason: A plan-like page restating, circa 1980–81, the genus-0 Teichmüller tower with S_ν × Γ action. This is material Grothendieck himself published in spirit in the Esquisse and the Longue Marche, and it is well developed in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. The only mildly notable details are the term 'groupe cartésien' for the contravariant functoriality in finite sets with monomorphisms, and the early date. Neither adds new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Top-right insertion is more plausibly 'en profini aussi' (fundamental groups trivial in the profinite sense too) than 'en propre aussi'.

'Le Type T_{0,ν} (ν ≥ 4) correspond au schéma des syst. de ν−3 points distincts' — the crossed-out fragment is 'est le topos fini…/groupe fini'; the 'étalé des' crossed text is likely 'étale de' or 'schéma des'.
'Son groupe fondamental est le complétifié profini d'un groupe de tresses Π_{0,ν}, lequel (comme tout "groupe cartésien") dépend contravariantement de [1,ν] pour les monomorphismes.'
'Sur les (T_{0,ν})_{Q̄} [or 'Les (T_{0,ν})_Q' with Q̄ inserted] on fait opérer S_ν, donc S_ν × Γ opère sur T_{0,ν},' — 'au fait opèrent' should read 'on fait opérer'.
